headline_phrase: Vitamin B12 deficiency in older adults produces neuropsychiatric presentations that are readily mistaken for primary psychiatric illness.
claim: Review of the neuropsychiatric manifestations of vitamin B12 deficiency in elderly patients, covering presentation, diagnosis and treatment.
journal: The Journal of Neuropsychiatry and Clinical Neurosciences
citation: Lachner C, Steinle NI, Regenold WT. The Neuropsychiatry of Vitamin B12 Deficiency in Elderly Patients. J Neuropsychiatry Clin Neurosci. 2012;24(1):5-15.
notes: Metadata verified against Crossref. Narrative review, so it summarizes the literature rather than testing anything.

headline_phrase: Frank folate deficiency has been under 1% of the US population since fortification. The often-quoted 20% figure is folate insufficiency in women of childbearing age, defined by neural tube defect risk, not by any mental health threshold.
population: US population, NHANES 1999-2016; insufficiency figures are women aged 12-49
n: 23684 serum and 24150 RBC samples in 2011-2016, ages 1 and over
claim: Folate deficiency (serum <7 nmol/L or RBC <305 nmol/L) was under 1% in persons aged 3 and over in every NHANES cycle from 1999 to 2016. Folate insufficiency (RBC <748 nmol/L, a neural tube defect risk threshold applied to women) was 18.6% in women aged 12 to 49 in 2011-2016 and 23.2% in 2007-2010.
journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
citation: Pfeiffer CM, Sternberg MR, Zhang M, Fazili Z, Storandt RJ, Crider KS. Folate status in the US population 20 y after the introduction of folic acid fortification. Am J Clin Nutr. 2019;110(5):1088-1097.
notes: Verified against the full text. The paper discusses neural tube defects only and contains no discussion of neuropsychiatric outcomes. Do not cite it as evidence that folate status affects mental health.

headline_phrase: Serum B12 alone misses deficiency. Methylmalonic acid and holotranscobalamin detect it earlier, which matters because the neurological damage can be irreversible.
population: Adults, with attention to elderly, vegetarians and people with gastrointestinal disease
claim: Review of the causes of B12 deficiency and of early diagnosis, arguing that holotranscobalamin and methylmalonic acid outperform total serum B12.
citation: Herrmann W, Obeid R. Causes and early diagnosis of vitamin B12 deficiency. Dtsch Arztebl Int. 2008;105(40):680-685.
notes: Verified. Sometimes cited as evidence that subclinical B12 deficiency has neuropsychiatric consequences. It is actually a review of causes and diagnosis, and supports the testing claim well and the neuropsychiatric claim only in passing.

headline_phrase: More than a quarter of people with neuropsychiatric damage from B12 deficiency had no anemia and no enlarged red cells, so a normal blood count does not rule it out.
claim: Of 141 consecutive patients with neuropsychiatric abnormality from cobalamin deficiency, 40 (28%) had neither anemia nor macrocytosis. All 39 evaluable patients improved on treatment.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
citation: Lindenbaum J et al. Neuropsychiatric disorders caused by cobalamin deficiency in the absence of anemia or macrocytosis. The New England journal of medicine. 1988;318:1720-8.
notes: Uncontrolled consecutive series. The response to treatment is what carries the causal weight.

headline_phrase: How severe the damage becomes tracks how long the diagnosis was missed, which is the most actionable finding in this whole area.
claim: Dementia, psychoses and mood disturbance documented. Hematocrit normal in 27%, mean cell volume normal in 23%. All 121 evaluable episodes responded, complete recovery in 47%.
citation: Healton EB et al. Neurologic aspects of cobalamin deficiency. Medicine. 1991;70:229-45.
notes: Severity before treatment tracked duration of symptoms before diagnosis.

headline_phrase: Four out of five confirmed Wernicke cases were never diagnosed while the patient was alive, and only 16% had the classic three symptoms.
claim: Of 131 necropsy-confirmed cases, 80% were undiagnosed in life, only 16% had the classic triad, and 19% had no documented clinical signs at all.
journal: Journal of neurology, neurosurgery, and psychiatry
citation: Harper CG et al. Clinical signs in the Wernicke-Korsakoff complex: a retrospective analysis of 131 cases diagnosed at necropsy. Journal of neurology, neurosurgery, and psychiatry. 1986;49:341-5.
notes: The triad is the exception, not the presentation. This is the single strongest argument for a low threshold to treat.

headline_phrase: Two of four signs is a better rule than waiting for the classic triad, and it was validated against autopsy findings.
claim: Operational criteria requiring two of four: dietary deficiency, eye movement abnormality, cerebellar dysfunction, or altered mental state or mild memory impairment.
journal: Journal of neurology, neurosurgery, and psychiatry
citation: Caine D et al. Operational criteria for the classification of chronic alcoholics: identification of Wernicke's encephalopathy. Journal of neurology, neurosurgery, and psychiatry. 1997;62:51-60.
notes: Adopted by European neurological guidance. Inter-rater reliability was complete across three raters.

headline_phrase: Pellagra was found at autopsy in 27% of people with chronic alcoholism and had been diagnosed in life in none of them, because most had no rash.
population: Necropsies of people with chronic alcoholism
claim: 20 of 74 necropsies showed pellagra. In none had the diagnosis been established clinically, because in the majority there were no skin lesions.
journal: Journal of neurology, neurosurgery, and psychiatry
citation: Ishii N et al. Pellagra among chronic alcoholics: clinical and pathological study of 20 necropsy cases. Journal of neurology, neurosurgery, and psychiatry. 1981;44:209-15.
notes: The origin of the phrase pellagra without the rash. Suspect it in alcohol dependence with mental or neurological symptoms even with normal skin.

headline_phrase: Alcoholic pellagra encephalopathy presents as confusion, rigidity and myoclonus, and is routinely missed because other alcohol-related conditions are present at the same time.
claim: Confusion or clouded consciousness, marked oppositional rigidity and myoclonus. Often unrecognized because other alcoholic encephalopathies coexisted.
citation: Serdaru M et al. The clinical spectrum of alcoholic pellagra encephalopathy. A retrospective analysis of 22 cases studied pathologically. Brain : a journal of neurology. 1988;111 ( Pt 4):829-42.
notes: Also reports that treating with thiamine and pyridoxine without niacin appeared to worsen 9 cases. The companion pathology paper on the same patients disagrees, so that part is not settled.

headline_phrase: The largest trial ever run found vitamin D did not prevent depression, in more than 18,000 adults followed over five years.
claim: 2000 IU daily vitamin D3 versus placebo, median 5.3 years. Depression or clinically relevant depressive symptoms hazard ratio 0.97. Mood score difference 0.01.
citation: Okereke OI et al. Effect of Long-term Vitamin D3 Supplementation vs Placebo on Risk of Depression or Clinically Relevant Depressive Symptoms and on Change in Mood Scores: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. 2020;324:471-480.
notes: Important limitation: only 2.4% of participants were deficient at baseline, so this tested supplementing replete people rather than correcting a deficiency.

headline_phrase: Intravenous iron genuinely helps restless legs syndrome, but at ferritin thresholds far above any definition of deficiency.
population: Adults with moderate to severe restless legs syndrome
claim: Task force review of 31 studies. Ferric carboxymaltose effective where ferritin is below 300, oral iron possibly effective at or below 75.
citation: Allen RP et al. Evidence-based and consensus clinical practice guidelines for the iron treatment of restless legs syndrome/Willis-Ekbom disease in adults and children: an IRLSSG task force report. Sleep medicine. 2018;41:27-44.
notes: Do not read this as restless legs being caused by iron deficiency. The thresholds are far above deficiency. Several antidepressants and antipsychotics aggravate the condition.

headline_phrase: Iron repletion reduced fatigue in non-anemic women with low iron, and did nothing at all for depression or anxiety.
population: Non-anemic menstruating women with ferritin below 50
claim: Fatigue fell significantly more on iron. No effect on depression (p = 0.97), anxiety (p = 0.5) or quality of life (p = 0.2), despite confirmed biochemical response.
journal: CMAJ : Canadian Medical Association journal = journal de l'Association medicale canadienne
citation: Vaucher P et al. Effect of iron supplementation on fatigue in nonanemic menstruating women with low ferritin: a randomized controlled trial. CMAJ : Canadian Medical Association journal = journal de l'Association medicale canadienne. 2012;184:1247-54.
notes: Closed-label with observer blinding only, so participants knew their allocation. A subjective-only benefit in a partly unblinded trial is what expectancy produces.

headline_phrase: The apparent benefit of magnesium for mood collapses once a placebo is introduced, from 1.60 standard deviations to 0.21.
claim: Uncontrolled trials give 1.60 standard deviations, placebo-controlled trials give 0.21. Blood magnesium in mood disorder patients was higher than controls. Prospective dietary association not significant.
citation: Phelan D et al. Magnesium and mood disorders: systematic review and meta-analysis. BJPsych open. 2018;4:167-179.
notes: Authors conclude there is little evidence for magnesium involvement in mood disorders. The design-dependence is the actual finding.

headline_phrase: Cochrane found a small effect of omega-3 on depression, called it unlikely to be clinically meaningful, and warned the estimate is probably biased toward a positive result.
claim: Standardized mean difference 0.40 across 33 studies, very low certainty. No effect on remission, response or quality of life. Funnel plot inspection suggests bias toward a positive finding.
journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
citation: Appleton KM et al. Omega-3 fatty acids for depression in adults. The Cochrane database of systematic reviews. 2021;11:CD004692.
notes: An effect of this size is about 2.5 points on a depression scale where the minimum clinically important change is 3.0.

headline_phrase: In the largest trial, people given omega-3 had a slightly higher risk of depression than people given placebo.
claim: 1 g daily fish oil versus placebo, median 5.3 years. Depression risk hazard ratio 1.13, statistically significant, in the direction of harm.
citation: Okereke OI et al. Effect of Long-term Supplementation With Marine Omega-3 Fatty Acids vs Placebo on Risk of Depression or Clinically Relevant Depressive Symptoms and on Change in Mood Scores: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. 2021;326:2385-2394.
notes: Authors conclude the findings do not support omega-3 to prevent depression. Ten times larger than the entire Cochrane placebo comparison.

headline_phrase: Proton pump inhibitors can cause severe magnesium depletion, proven by symptoms resolving within days of stopping and returning within days of restarting.
population: Adults on long-term proton pump inhibitors
claim: Median onset 5.5 years of use, range 14 days to 13 years. Recovery a median 4 days after stopping, recurrence within 4 days on restarting. Switching to an H2 blocker prevented recurrence.
citation: Hess MW et al. Systematic review: hypomagnesaemia induced by proton pump inhibition. Alimentary pharmacology & therapeutics. 2012;36:405-13.
notes: Rare. Roughly 30 published cases against about 21 million annual US users. The rechallenge data is what makes it causal rather than associated.

headline_phrase: Metformin lowers vitamin B12 by about a fifth over four years, with one extra deficiency for every 14 people treated.
claim: Randomized, 4.3 years. B12 fell 19%. Absolute risk of B12 below 150 pmol/L 7.2 percentage points higher, number needed to harm 13.8.
citation: de Jager J et al. Long term treatment with metformin in patients with type 2 diabetes and risk of vitamin B-12 deficiency: randomised placebo controlled trial. BMJ (Clinical research ed.). 2010;340:c2181.
notes: The best-established drug and nutrient pair here. Note that no study has tested whether this affects mood or cognition.

headline_phrase: Adding folic acid to antidepressants did not help, and the treated group scored slightly worse on mental health.
population: Adults with depression, folate-deficient people excluded
claim: 5 mg folic acid added to antidepressants, 12 weeks, followed to 25 weeks. Null on every outcome. Mental health score significantly reduced by 3.0%.
citation: Bedson E et al. Folate Augmentation of Treatment--Evaluation for Depression (FolATED): randomised trial and economic evaluation. Health technology assessment (Winchester, England). 2014;18:vii-viii, 1-159.
notes: Authors state the finding undermines guidelines advocating folic acid for depression. The largest augmentation trial in this literature.

headline_phrase: How common B12 deficiency looks depends almost entirely on which cutoff you pick: the same survey gives anywhere from 3% to 26%.
population: US adults aged 19 and over, NHANES 1999-2004
claim: Commonly used serum cutoffs give 3% to 26%. Functional marker cutoffs give 2% to 6%. Requiring both abnormal gives about 1% with clear deficiency and 92% adequate.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
citation: Bailey RL et al. Monitoring of vitamin B-12 nutritional status in the United States by using plasma methylmalonic acid and serum vitamin B-12. The American journal of clinical nutrition. 2011;94:552-61.
notes: Any single prevalence figure quoted without its cutoff is meaningless. This paper is the clearest demonstration of why.

headline_phrase: After gastric bypass, people using a vitamin patch had roughly twice the rate of deficiency of people taking pills.
population: Patients one year after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
claim: 82% of patch users had at least one deficiency at one year against 41% of pill users. Significantly lower vitamin D, B1 and B12 in the patch group.
citation: Saurabh S et al. Is Transdermal Multivitamin Patch Effective in Gastric Bypass Patients?. Obesity surgery. 2019;29:3818-3823.
notes: Retrospective chart review of self-selected patients at one hospital, not a trial. Direction is clear, design is weak.

headline_phrase: The only large randomized test of nutrients absorbed through the skin found essentially nothing, in 444 infants over a year.
population: Infants randomized at 4 to 7 weeks, followed to 12 months
claim: Liposomal iron, vitamin D, folate and B12 in massage oil versus placebo oil. No hemoglobin benefit. Vitamin D difference 1.46 ng/mL, which the authors call marginal. No developmental difference.
citation: Apte A et al. Efficacy of transdermal delivery of liposomal micronutrients through body oil massage on neurodevelopmental and micronutrient deficiency status in infants: results of a randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial. BMC nutrition. 2021;7:48.
notes: The strongest single study of transdermal micronutrient delivery in humans, and it is largely null.

headline_phrase: Vitamin D deficiency peaks in adults aged 20 to 39, which is the opposite of what most people assume.
claim: At risk of deficiency below 30 nmol/L: 5.0%. At risk of inadequacy 30 to 49 nmol/L: 18.3%. Deficiency peaks at 7.6% in those aged 20 to 39 and is 2.9% in those 60 and over.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
citation: Herrick KA et al. Vitamin D status in the United States, 2011-2014. The American journal of clinical nutrition. 2019;110:150-157.
notes: The age pattern matters because it overlaps the band where psychiatric prescribing is heaviest.

headline_phrase: Five out of six people with iron deficiency are not anemic, so screening on hemoglobin misses most of them.
claim: Among those with iron deficiency, 83.6% did not have anemia. Prevalence 17.0% at a ferritin cutoff of 15, 38.6% at 25, and 77.5% at 50.
citation: Weyand AC et al. Prevalence of Iron Deficiency and Iron-Deficiency Anemia in US Females Aged 12-21 Years, 2003-2020. JAMA. 2023;329:2191-2193.
notes: The clearest demonstration that the cutoff decides the answer more than the population does.

headline_phrase: A review of the field concludes that the promotion of transdermal magnesium is scientifically unsupported.
citation: Gröber U et al. Myth or Reality-Transdermal Magnesium?. Nutrients. 2017;9.
notes: End-to-end test of the automatic intake.
